newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil trade deficit not seen affecting growth.
newsitem.headline: Brazil trade deficit not seen affecting growth.

text.p: Brazil's trade deficit so far this year of $937 million does not represent an obstacle to economic growth, said Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, eccnomic policy secretary at the Finance Ministry.

Mendonca de Barros said the government was not concerned about August's $291 million deficit because imports were healthy and a bill passed Thursday by the Senate exempting some exports from so-called ICMS taxes was expected to boost shipments.
"The trade balance shouldn't be seen as an obstacle to economic growth," he told reporters.

Mendonca de Barros said imports of primary and intermediary goods had risen to $2.238 billion in August from $2.224 billion in July but that imports of consumer goods were stable month-on-month at $896 million versus $890 million in July.
"That signals internal production is growing," he said.

The economic policy secretary, regarded as number two in the Finance Ministry, said exporters had been holding up shipments in anticipation of the vote in the Senate on the bill exempting primary and some semi-manufatured goods from ICMS export tax.
He said he expected exports to resume with the publication of the law in the Official Journal, expected to occur within the next few days.
"Our evaluation of the ICMS vote is positive for sugar, coffee, oranges, aluminium and meat exports," he said.
